comparisons.peer_summary: AMD had $5.0 billion in unconditional purchase commitments as of December 28, 2024, primarily for wafer and substrate purchases, with $4.5 billion due in fiscal year 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific unconditional purchase obligations for property, plant, and equipment or wafer/substrate commitments in the current year. MU reports $1.17 billion in purchase obligations for PP&E as of August 29, 2024, with $1.10 billion due within one year. AMD reports $5.0 billion in unconditional purchase commitments as of December 28, 2024, with $4.5 billion due in fiscal year 2025. sentences.text: To develop new product and process technology, support future growth, achieve operating efficiencies, and maintain product quality, we must continue to invest in manufacturing technologies, facilities and equipment, and R&D. We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be around mid-30% range of revenue for the year.
We expect capital expenditures to be higher in the fiscal year ending November 2, 2025 as compared to fiscal year 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, the company had $14.0 billion in capital expenditure commitments for 2025 and $6.0 billion long-term, alongside $2.1 billion in other purchase obligations for 2025 and $4.9 billion long-term.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific capital expenditure commitments and other purchase obligations for the upcoming fiscal year. MU estimates its 2025 capital expenditures to be in the mid-30% range of revenue, supported by $1.17 billion in purchase obligations for PP&E as of August 29, 2024. INTC had $14.0 billion in capital expenditure commitments for 2025 and $6.0 billion in long-term commitments as of December 28, 2024, alongside $2.1 billion in other purchase obligations for 2025. Both provide specific forward-looking commitment amounts for the next fiscal year, although INTC's scale is substantially larger.

sentences.text: To develop new product and process technology, support future growth, achieve operating efficiencies, and maintain product quality, we must continue to invest in manufacturing technologies, facilities and equipment, and R&D. We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be around mid-30% range of revenue for the year.

As of August 29, 2024, we had purchase obligations of approximately $1.17 billion for the acquisition of property, plant, and equipment, of which approximately $1.10 billion is expected to be paid within one year.

• Our purchase obligations at September 29, 2024, which primarily relate to purchase commitments with certain suppliers of our integrated circuit products, including those under multi-year capacity commitments, totaled $12.8 billion, of which, $9.6 billion is expected to be paid in the next 12 months.

• Cash outflows for capital expenditures were $1.0 billion in fiscal 2024 and $1.5 billion in fiscal 2023. We expect capital expenditures to increase from fiscal 2024 in the near term to support our production and testing needs related to our growth and diversification initiatives.
